description: Explore the best construction logos in 2026. Get inspired by strong brand designs from leading construction companies.
body:
‍Construction logos are more than just symbols. They are the face of a company that builds dreams and shapes landscapes.

The best construction logos tend to be the ones that reflect the vision, mission, and values of the company.

The image of a construction company can make or break its reputation in the industry.

A well-designed logo communicates professionalism, reliability, and the essence of the business.

This article explores some of the most impressive logos of construction companies, revealing how they combine design and originality with the solid world of construction.

‍12 Best Examples of Construction Company Logos

  1. Turner Construction
  2. Gilbane 
  3. Skanska
  4. Kiewit 
  5. Balfour Beatty
  6. Whiting-Turner
  7. TutorPerini
  8. AECOM
  9. PCL
  10. Fluor Corporation
  11. Jacobs Solutions
  12.  McDermott

Most of the logos below, use bold type and other visual elements that stand for strength, stability and precision.

1. Turner Construction

Turner Construction is a well-established American construction company that has been in business since 1902 and has a global presence in 20 countries. 

Its logo is a heavy sans serif-style wordmark, which appears to be a modified version of Helvetica Black.

The name is set in a strong, deep blue color, which typically conveys reliability and professionalism.

The first letter is uppercase, with following "u" tucked in—which may represent precision and stability, key attributes for a construction company.

There's no extra embellishment or graphic, suggesting a straightforward, no-nonsense approach to their work.

The design is simple, clean, and modern, which aids in easy recognition and suggests efficiency and clarity in the company's identity.

Overall, this extremely bold typography, together with the dark blue creates a clean professional appearance.

‍2. Gilbane

Gilbane is a family-owned and highly regarded American construction company started in 1870 by William H. Gilbane and his brother.

This logo features the word "Gilbane" in bold sans-serif font, with the first "G" letter left outside of a red rectangle.

The primary color is a vibrant red, which often signifies energy, passion, and action.

This color choice might also be intended to grab attention and stand out among competitors (most use blue or black).

I really like the red rectangle with the name (besides "G") in negative space—it makes for a very unique visual element.

Overall, the simplicity of the design allows for versatility and easy recognition, important for a strong corporate identity.

3. Skanska

Skanska, a Swedish construction corporation, is one of the industry's largest brands.

Skanska's logo communicates thoughts of refinement and credibility.

The logo is a simple wordmark in all uppercase characters in a pretty unique sans-serif font (with slight curves).

The dark blue color emphasizes the company's dedication to credible, and dependable service. 

With such strong brand recognition, they have no problem relying on a simple wordmark design to send their message.

4. Kiewit

Kiewit caters to the transportation, oil and gas, electrical, power, and waterworks industries.

‍Peter Kiewit Sons, Inc. was formed in 1884 and is currently owned by the Kiewit family members.

Kiewit's logo consists of the initials of the company name in a badge with the founding year.

The company boasts one of the industry's brightest and most eye-catching logos, which is depicted in black and yellow. 

The logo itself represents strength, recognition, and heritage.

Kiewit's color choices are directly related to the construction sector, which frequently uses black and yellow on safety signs and products. ‍ 

5. Balfour Beatty

Balfour Beatty is an international infrastructure firm headquartered in the United Kingdom.

Balfour Betty was created in 1909 and is named after its original founders. 

The company's name is conveyed through its simple but appealing logo, which is designed using a condensed sans-serif font with very tight kerning.

With a dark blue color palette and a powerful font style that is easy to read, the Balfour Beatty logo can be quickly recognized.

The powerful typeface, paired with the color blue, convey notions of solidity and strength.

As you can see, construction companies often opt for a strong sans serif (almost blocky) typefaces and often blue color.

6. Whiting-Turner

Whiting-Turner offers construction management, general contracting, and design-build services to a wide range of clients.

Their logo contains of the initials "WT" with a bold underline underneath.

Orange is a fantastic choice for a construction logo since it demonstrates the company's commitment to safety (and it's pretty distinctive too).

The WT symbol is an eye-catching that helps the company stand out from a distance.

7. TutorPerini

Tutor Perini was founded in 1894 and is headquartered in Sylmar, California.

Tutor Perini, like many of the largest construction businesses, utilizes a simple wordmark for their logo.

The first part of the company name is set in gray and the second part in green, which creates a nice contrast between the two.

The font used in this logo appears to be Helvetica Neue Black, which has a powerful presence and is ideal for construction industry.

The logotype uses a tight kerning, which makes the logo look robust, and even though Helvetica has been around for a long time, it has a modern appearance.

The color gray is frequently linked with sophistication and professionalism, whereas green denotes growth and sustainability. 

8. AECOM

AECOM (American engineering, infrastructure, and consulting firm) is one of the largest construction firms in the US.

AECOM's logo design is modern, with a stylized wordmark logo. 

The logo is based on the Futura PT Heavy Oblique (Italic) font, with the letter "E" missing the stem and instead with just a sequence of lines.

This possibly indicates the company's devotion to moving other businesses into the future. 

Black is a fairly simple color that shows the brand's refinement and professionalism.

‍9. PCL

PCL was established in 1906 and incorporated in 1913 as Poole Construction Company Limited. 

This oval shaped logo stands out because of clever design and color palette.

The logo is intended to be noticeable anywhere it appears, from hard hats to brochure designs.

The green and yellow colors contrast wonderfully and create an eye-catching combo.

Additionally, the yellow outline highlights characteristics such as security, continuity, and safety.

This logo is very simple yet highly appealing, and I'd say very different from the rest—as others mainly use squares and rectangles, not ovals.

10. Fluor Corporation

Fluor Corporation is an American multinational engineering and construction firm headquartered in Irving, Texas

Fluor is also named after its founders, and the company's logo is also a simple wordmark (like many above).

Fluor employs Tarzana Wide Bold Italic for their wordmark, which is such a unique font that it does not require many changes to appear good.

The Flour wordmark is properly spaced out to be legible across all mediums.

It also has a tiny flourish on the "R" to show originality. 

The color blue reflects the company's devotion to credibility and trust. 

‍11. Jacobs Solutions

Jacobs Solutions Inc. is an American companyprovides engineering, technical, professional and construction services

The logo consists of a wordmark of the company name with a stylized letter "J" and a curved line that can depict a bridge, or a road.

The separation in the "J" also cleverly creates a simple arrow shape pointing upward and to the right.

The integrated letter and arrow logo effectively communicates the company's strategic vision and skills across many technical disciplines.

Th use of a simple black-and-white color palette, reflects Jacobs' commitment to plain solutions and transparent communication. 

Overall, this smart logo design captures the Jacobs brand identity: professional, innovative, focused, and poised to guide clients into the future. 

‍12. McDermott

McDermott has designed and built comprehensive oil and gas infrastructure and technology for years.

Their logo is wonderfully done, and the green outline underneath the brand name adds an intriguing touch it.

The green outline demonstrates their capacity to complete a job from beginning to end.

It also helps to focus attention on the wordmark that is set in a simple middle-weight sans serif uppercase font.

It's also visually appealing how it frames the “M” in an alternative and shorter form of the logo.

I really like this original approach, the blue and green contrast is also particularly stunning, making the logo look iconic.

Conclusion

In conclusion, the logos of construction companies serve as a visual keystone, embodying the essence of each firm's values, vision, and commitment to excellence.

From Turner's bold blue typography to Gilbane's energetic red and Skanska's dynamic curves—these logos are meticulously crafted to stand as beacons of strength, precision, and professionalism.

They transcend mere graphic design to become symbols of the monumental works these companies construct, shaping skylines and realizing dreams.

Whether it’s through memorable names, iconic logos, or striking fonts, these companies have been able to show excellence in branding.
